title: Basic
summary: Toolchain, types, ownership, borrowing, enums and error handling: the ideas you need before writing any real Rust.
intro: Rust looks familiar at first glance: functions, structs, loops, generics. The real difference is that the compiler tracks who owns every value and for how long. This track builds that mental model, step by step, contrasting it with garbage-collected and manually managed languages.

concepts.title: Compiled ahead of time
concepts.text: rustc produces a native binary through LLVM. There is no VM and no JIT: what you ship is machine code plus a statically linked standard library.

concepts.title: No garbage collector
concepts.text: Every value has exactly one owner. When the owner goes out of scope the value is dropped, deterministically, at a point you can read in the source code.

concepts.title: Move by default
concepts.text: Assignment and argument passing move heap-owning values instead of copying or sharing them. Cheap stack-only types opt into Copy.

concepts.title: Aliasing XOR mutability
concepts.text: At any time you can have many shared references (&T) or exactly one mutable reference (&mut T), never both. This single rule rules out data races and iterator invalidation.

concepts.title: Expressions everywhere
concepts.text: if, match and blocks are expressions that produce values. Combined with enums, this replaces null, exceptions and many design patterns.

concepts.title: Errors in the type system
concepts.text: Fallible functions return Result<T, E>. The ? operator propagates errors explicitly; panics are reserved for bugs.
